claims_disputed.claim: Memory-architecture rankings depend on the probe LLM.
claims_disputed.reason: The Grok-side ranking being 'reordered' was never established: in Table 2, Mem0 answer accuracy 32.4 [25.2, 40.5] and cited Markdown 24.5 [18.2, 32.1] have overlapping Wilson CIs. The Bayesian paired test in §4.7 compares Gemini vs Grok within each system, not file memory vs Mem0 under Gemini, so the claimed rank flip is untested. That Gemini improves some systems is moderate; that the ranking depends on the LLM is weak.

claims_disputed.claim: Most tasks are solvable when relevant facts are visible; more context is not automatically better.
claims_disputed.reason: The first half holds (83.2% oracle, §4.5). The second half is largely a construction artifact: durable facts are seeded only in user turns (§3.2), and assistant replies were generated by an agent that could not see cross-session facts, so they can assert facts are 'absent from the model' (§5). Adding those replies injects contradictions built into the benchmark. §4.4 and §5 concede the analogous ingestion-scope result is 'partly a consequence of the benchmark design'.

pattern_stance_changes.reason: The LLM judge is the paper's measuring instrument, not a harness component compared against an alternative. Validation is one expert on 40 tasks with a same-family (Grok-4.3) judge (§3.3, §5). That is measurement hygiene, not evidence that an LLM judge or reviewer improves an agent workflow.

missed_issues: Scope of the P07 'contradicts': the graph is Graphiti's conversation-memory temporal KG at default ontology (§3.4, §4.6 skips customising it). It says nothing about code or knowledge graphs for code context. Graphiti's coverage deficit vs Mem0 is CI-separated (R-cov 27.3 [20.6, 35.1] vs 49.3 [41.2, 57.4]), but its answer accuracy is not below uncited Markdown (21.0 vs 17.6).
Domain-customisation results (§4.6, Fig. 3) are reported only graphically, with no CIs or test, from a single run; 'brings file memory roughly level with Mem0' cannot be checked from the text.

In §4.7 the Grok-4.3 judge scores both the Grok and Gemini agents. Self-preference would bias against Gemini (so its gain is conservative), but it also means the main-table system ranking is graded by the same model that wrote the memories.
Single run at temperature 0 per configuration; Wilson CIs capture task-sampling noise only, not run-to-run agent variance.
note: I agree with admit_with_caveats; the review is careful and its scores are within one point of mine. Two claims overreach what the CIs and benchmark construction allow (the rank flip is untested, and 'more context hurts' is partly a construction artifact). The LLM-judge stance should be neutral because the judge is the instrument, not the intervention.
